Maintenance Report — MNT-0066-003

Asset: WELL-0066 (SW-24 Well 066, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 07 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 26 Apr 2023 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 454 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0066-0023 on 2023-04-06 Report written: 27 Apr 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0066-0023 showed the wellhead at 18.9 °C with the air at 16.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0066-005

Asset: WELL-0066 (SW-24 Well 066, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 12 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 12 May 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0066-0028 on 2023-05-11 Report written: 13 May 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0066-0028 at 12:30 on 2023-05-11 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.8% of the pad area, estimated 1.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 205 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 164 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0066-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.64% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0066-011

Asset: WELL-0066 (SW-24 Well 066, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 10 Nov 2023 08:00 · Finished: 14 Nov 2023 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 102 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0066-0054 on 2023-11-09 Report written: 15 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0066-0054 showed the wellhead at 22.6 °C with the air at 18.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0066-031

Asset: WELL-0066 (SW-24 Well 066, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 24 Apr 2026 08:00 · Finished: 29 Apr 2026 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 116 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0066-0180 on 2026-04-23 Report written: 29 Apr 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0066-0180 showed the wellhead at 27.8 °C with the air at 24.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.
